open_points.subject: Network topology for services other than Client Portal
open_points.text: the service API for services, reachable only on the production host and over the protected channel (R0-28)
open_points.question: Where do PresuPro, Cabinet and Cabinet Kernel run, and how do they reach the production Registry? The WireGuard tunnel is described only for Portal, and no agent runs on the home server.
options: all of them run on the home server
they share the VPS WireGuard tunnel
each host gets its own protected channel
open_points.default_guess: Services on the VPS use the same home-initiated WireGuard tunnel, each with its own token; Kernel runs where the agent runs and reaches Registry over that tunnel.

open_points.subject: Owner interface remote reachability
open_points.text: the owner interface, reachable remotely only through HTTPS (R0-29)
open_points.question: From where is the owner interface reachable remotely: the home LAN, a VPN, or the public internet through a port the home server publishes? R0-39 says the home server publishes no listening port to the internet.
options: home LAN only
through the WireGuard tunnel / a VPN
public internet via a reverse proxy on the VPS
open_points.default_guess: Home LAN and owner VPN only, with no port published to the internet.

open_points.subject: Test instances
open_points.text: Test instances — any other instance ... Each holds its own identity space and no production personal data
open_points.question: Do test instances also require authentication, serve the owner interface, and hold their own secrets? Secrets and the network surface are described for production only.
options: same authentication rules as production with their own secrets
relaxed rules allowed on test instances
open_points.default_guess: Same rules as production, with secrets distinct from production's.

open_points.subject: Customer field in context vs contact data reaching owner alone
open_points.text: The customer's contact data reaches the owner alone.
open_points.question: Does the `customer` field of `context`, served to PresuPro and Client Portal, carry only the customer_ref or any contact data (for example the name)?
options: customer_ref only
customer_ref and name
full contact data for personal_data tokens
open_points.default_guess: customer_ref only; contact data reaches only the owner.

open_points.subject: restrict processing of a customer
open_points.text: its contact data stays stored but leaves Registry to no one but the owner (R0-37)
open_points.question: What does a restriction change in observable behaviour, given that contact data already reaches the owner alone? Does it block naming the customer in projects, the customer_ref in `context`, or something else?
options: it blocks customer_ref in context and new project links
it is only a recorded flag
it blocks corrections
open_points.default_guess: Record the flag; a restricted customer's ref is withheld from service answers and new projects may not name it.

open_points.subject: publish / withdraw an artifact pointer by Kernel for the agent
open_points.text: publish an artifact pointer | producer service; the owner for any owner service
open_points.question: Are publish and withdraw by Kernel confined to the session's project (R0-41), with a failure for another project? The table states no such confinement or failure for either action.
options: confined to the session's project with an explicit refusal
Kernel publishes unconfined as a producer
open_points.default_guess: Confined to the session's project; another project is refused.

open_points.subject: read the latest artifact of a type
open_points.text: read the latest artifact of a type | owner; a service
open_points.question: Can Kernel for the agent read the latest pointer of any project, or only of its session's project as R0-41 and R0-32 require?
options: session's project only
any project
open_points.default_guess: Session's project only for Kernel; other services are limited by their token.

open_points.subject: read a project / list projects for a non-personal_data service
open_points.text: owner; a trusted service, in its disclosure class (R0-26)
open_points.question: What project card and list items does a service whose token stops below personal_data receive (object, address, customer, name)? R0-26 forbids mixed answers.
options: a projection without personal fields
refused entirely
open_points.default_guess: A separate projection without object or customer fields.

open_points.subject: choose the working project / agent sessions
open_points.question: How does Registry learn of agent sessions, and how does the owner see which sessions exist in order to choose for one? No action registers or lists sessions.
options: Kernel registers a session as an action
the session appears with its first context read or switch request
the owner types the session id
open_points.default_guess: Kernel announces a session through a declared action; the owner interface lists the known sessions.

open_points.subject: request a project switch
open_points.text: request a project switch ... unknown project refused
open_points.question: How does the agent name a target project without seeing the catalogue, and does answering 'unknown project' reveal to the agent which ids exist?
options: the agent names a free-text hint and the owner picks the project
the agent names an id and gets no existence signal
open_points.default_guess: The agent sends an id or hint; Registry accepts it without revealing existence, and the owner resolves it.

open_points.subject: list pending switch requests
open_points.text: a pending request of that session the owner sees in the owner interface
open_points.question: Which action lets the owner list the pending switch requests and sessions (R0-29 switch-request view)?
options: add 'list switch requests' for the owner
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner action that lists pending requests per session.

open_points.subject: import a project with its identity
open_points.text: with its customer, object, rooms and pointers (R0-34, R0-44)
open_points.question: Does import keep the source's customer_ref and pointer and room ids, contrary to R0-16 (Registry mints customer_ref, never caller-supplied), or are new ones minted and remapped?
options: keep all source ids
keep project_id only and remint the others
open_points.default_guess: Keep project_id and room ids; remint customer_ref and pointer ids under the owner's mapping check.

open_points.subject: end of a customer relationship
open_points.text: A customer's contact data: until the relationship with the customer ends, plus one year.
open_points.question: Which action records that a relationship ended, starting the retention clock? Its representation is carried to State 1, but no primary action carries it.
options: an owner action 'end relationship'
derived from all of the customer's projects being archived
open_points.default_guess: Derived from the archiving of the customer's last project, with an owner override.

open_points.subject: Audit: significant operations
open_points.text: Every significant operation leaves an audit entry
open_points.question: Which operations are significant: all writes, reads of personal data, refusals, context reads? This is not carried to a later state.
options: every write and every personal_data read and every refusal
writes only
open_points.default_guess: Every write, every personal_data read, every working-context change and every authorization refusal.

open_points.subject: What Registry stores
open_points.text: Registry stores identity, the owner's choice of working project and pointers only.
open_points.question: Does the statement include the Customer contact data, the switch requests and the audit log that the decisions require Registry to keep?
options: extend the statement
treat them as part of identity
open_points.default_guess: Extend the statement to name customer records, switch requests and the audit log.

open_points.subject: Display name classification in agent projection
open_points.text: id, display name, status, rooms and artifact pointers
open_points.question: A project name often contains an address or a customer surname. Is the display name non-personal, and how is that guaranteed?
options: the name is business_confidential and the owner avoids personal values
a separate agent-safe label
open_points.default_guess: The display name is business_confidential; the owner interface warns against personal values in it.

open_points.subject: onboard_object
open_points.text: The operator script `onboard_object`: a client of the API like any consumer
open_points.question: With every request authenticated (R0-27) and the owner credential held by no tool (R0-30), does onboard_object get a service token, or is it retired?
options: retired
given its own service token
open_points.default_guess: Retired; its role passes to the owner interface and Kernel.

open_points.subject: Cabinet Web mirror
open_points.text: Consumer services — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, the Cabinet Web mirror. Each authenticates with its own service token
open_points.question: Does the Cabinet Web mirror get a token? R0-27 leaves it conditional.
options: it gets a read-only token
it loses access
open_points.default_guess: It loses access until the owner issues a token.

open_points.subject: R0-45 acceptance
open_points.text: proposed to the owner 2026-10-27 after round 3 T8, T11, T12, no objection
open_points.question: Is a proposal met with no objection an owner decision of the same standing as the other R0 entries?
options: yes, binding
provisional until the owner accepts the whole
open_points.default_guess: Binding, and confirmed when the owner accepts the whole.
